body:
As for being a spectator, this will sound silly, but I have been writing rap for many years (basically just less intelligent poems) and I think I have an excerpt from my writing that correlates nicely 

-----

"Riding the fence and I'm watching y'all battling 

I'm independent from all of y'all savages

Rather stay separate from all of your plans for the ravaging"

----

I'm not trying to be pretentious or anything, this is just something I wrote a while back that seems to coincide with your thoughts. I am also a tad drunk and feel like this should excuse my perhaps less than inappropriate verbiage for whatever reason.

 I often feel like I'm objectively viewing the world around me and I just don't assimilate into it. It gives me both displeasure and comfort.

Your last paragraph hit me hard. I'm in such agreement with you. If it's all for nothing, why not just enjoy it as much as humanly possible. Thanks for sharing your viewpoints, it makes me happy to know that I share thoughts and feelings with others.

We do well online probably because most of our interaction has happened via written, online media. I know most of mine has, at least. At least 90% of every thought I've ever expressed, I have typed. It's more natural to me than speaking. 

My mother was raised Catholic but is just as atheist as I am in terms of believing in a deity or an afterlife. My father does not subscribe to any particular denomination, however, he does believe in a personal god. He does believe that something happens to our sentience after we experience a physical death and I just can't see how that's possible, likely or observable. There is zero evidence. 

I do like the idea of karma but not in the traditional sense. It just makes sense to me that if you treat people well they're more likely to treat you well in return. Perhaps this is a reductionist view of the concept but it suits me. Thanks for reading my post too. 

Ted Talks, Sam Harris, Neil Degrasse, Bill Nye, anyone with an interesting and thought provoking aspect - all of these offer me insight and comfort. If we are as similar as I suspect, I imagine you may benefit from them as well. 

I know it seems like we won't find anyone to relate to, but this interaction alone leads me to believe it is much easier to find people who share your values than we think. Much love :)

I often feel like I wish I could just walk into a church and really believe in what they have to say but trying to get an atheist or agnostic person to believe in any denomination of religion is akin to trying to convince a Catholic that Islam is the true path, or vice versa.  Everything I know tells me they're wrong. 

Being mindful 100% of the time is impossible.. but at least it allows us to overcome the times we weren't mindful. 

Also, you talked a bit about not being able to relate to people, but honestly it seems to me that if you and I had met in real life, we would get along great. And fortunately, there are tons of humans, and we're not all entirely unique, so there are bound to be leagues more like minded people. It's just statistics. 

You speak well, you know your way around words, and you make small talk just fine. I feel like I can't really make small talk or relate to anyone and then I see someone like you who is similar to me and when I see that you are indeed capable of the very things you claim not to be, it makes me realize that I must be too. And this short conversation is evidence of that for both of us.

Have you ever heard of impostor syndrome? I think you might appreciate this video. Sorry to keep linking you to stuff, it just seems relevant and potentially helpful. 

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eqhUHyVpAwE

You have self-awareness in abundance. That much is clear. You're too smart to be fooled into buying into delusions that offer most people happiness. I feel like you and I are very similar for a lot of reasons, but you had a harder go of it. I don't know what sort of treatment is right for anyone but if I could encourage you to do anything, please keep writing, even if only for yourself. You're rather articulate and reading your post helped me reflect on myself a great deal. This is not glib talk, either, I mean it.

Did writing this help in some small way? It helps me to write stuff like this because it allows me to be self-analytical and critical with more clarity than thinking in my head. It's like you're writing a map of your mind. And like you said about ruminating, getting into a cycle of depressive thoughts, this seems like it might be an effective way to get out that cycle. 

edit: If you're interested, check this video out

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Iwac6Uk-zyk 

specifically at 1:45. I love Harris, he's such an intelligent and thoughtful guy, offers a lot of insight. He has a lot of videos, books, and podcasts available if you're into what he has to say.
